ownership.cpu_archive: CPU BF16 K/V owned by CompressedHistoryArchive records
ownership.gpu_lowbit: Per-record gpu_k_payload/gpu_v_payload plus metadata; created lazily on first non-promoted selected fetch and retained in the record
ownership.local: cache[k]/cache[v], persistent dense BF16 local window
ownership.transient: BF16 promotion and dequantized low-bit materializations returned by materialize_selected

sparse_order: Q-sparse selection occurs before CompressedHistoryArchive.materialize_selected; materialize_selected then splits retained IDs into promoted CPU BF16 and low-bit GPU dequant paths.

sparsity_effect.reason: Only selected IDs are materialized per call, but once a selected low-bit record is created, its GPU payload remains attached to the archive record. The code has no per-ratio eviction of gpu_k_payload/gpu_v_payload; archive eviction is tied to rolling history records, not Q-sparse ratio.

memory_accounting.GPU_KV_MEASURED_BYTES: cache[k]/cache[v] storage only, deduplicated by storage identity; current local dense BF16 KV
memory_accounting.GPU_PACKED_K_BYTES: sum of persistent rec.gpu_k_payload values for records whose low-bit owner has been created
memory_accounting.GPU_PACKED_V_BYTES: sum of persistent rec.gpu_v_payload values for records whose low-bit owner has been created
memory_accounting.GPU_PACKED_SCALE_BYTES: payload scale/amax and record metadata tensor storage where discoverable
memory_accounting.GPU_KV_BF16_EQUIVALENT_BYTES: logical BF16 size for every archive record shape plus local BF16 cache; this is an estimate/equivalent, not an allocation measurement
memory_accounting.TRANSIENT_DEQUANT_GPU_PEAK_BYTES: cache counters updated from returned BF16 dequant tensors
memory_accounting.TRANSIENT_PROMOTION_GPU_PEAK_BYTES: cache counters updated from promoted CPU BF16 H2D materializations
memory_accounting.PEAK_GPU_ALLOCATED_BYTES: not produced by runtime_inference_memory; must come from separate torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated instrumentation if needed

source_locations.q_sparse_then_materialize: wan/modules/causal_model_latentmem.py:1264-1298 and the archive materialization path in the attention retrieval block

reported_numeric_rows.finding: The current source defines no retained-ratio memory formula that produces these rows. Several matching decimals (for example 3.2270, 2.6303, 1.5181, 1.0684) occur in profiling CSVs as timing fields such as time_score_ms or EXPOSED_CRITICAL_PATH_TIME, not as GPU memory fields. They must not be reported as GiB without the originating table/artifact.

semantic_verdict.current_problem: The field name is too broad: GPU_KV_MEASURED_BYTES is local dense BF16 KV, while GPU_KV_ACTUAL_PERSISTENT_BYTES includes local dense KV plus persistent low-bit owners but does not expose the historical persistent component separately. It also does not expose active working-set bytes as a separate field.

final_answers.1: Current Group14/15 GPU_KV_MEASURED is local dense BF16 KV, not historical packed KV. Historical packed ownership is represented separately by GPU_PACKED_K/V fields when populated.
final_answers.2: Q-sparsity definitely reduces active materialized working set. It does not necessarily physically reduce persistent GPU packed storage after selected records have been lazily cached.
final_answers.3: Previously selected/pruned-by-Q chunks can still have persistent GPU packed K/V if they were selected in an earlier call; Q-pruned chunks are not packed merely because they were pruned in the current call.
final_answers.4: For the corrected path, Q-sparse selection precedes materialize_selected. Low-bit packing is lazy on first selected non-promoted fetch, not a full pre-pack of every historical chunk.
final_answers.5: Yes. The per-record gpu_k_payload/gpu_v_payload fields form a lazy persistent resident cache. No ratio-based eviction is present; history eviction removes archive records.
final_answers.6: The four Group14 numbers cannot be validated as GiB from current memory artifacts; their matching decimals appear in timing traces. Treat their memory label as unverified/mislabelled.
final_answers.7: The four Group15 numbers have the same problem; current source does not define a formula yielding them as GiB.
final_answers.8: No. GPU_KV_ACTUAL_PERSISTENT_BYTES is closer to local dense plus currently materialized persistent low-bit payloads, but it is not decomposed enough to be an authoritative historical/persistent semantic field.
final_answers.9: Final tables should use the recommended fields separately; never use GPU_KV_MEASURED_BYTES as historical GPU KV and never fold transient BF16 buffers into persistent KV.
